title: How to get Modern Interiors working in MZ

posts.author: OroborosGames
posts.body:
Hello,
I recently decided to start developing a game and found a tileset collection I really like (
https://limezu.itch.io/moderninteriors
). However, when I import the tilesets I want to use into RMMZ, not all the assets on the sheet are available, it appears to get cut off. Is there a way to get all assets on the sheet available from the tileset menu so I can place them on the map?
Thanks for any advice!

I have this set because I figured I could use it as a cheap template for furniture edits and here's what it says
RPG MAKER MV/MZ MANUAL
--
1)IMPORTING WALLS AND FLOORS
- Create a new project on the RPG_MAKER
- On the upper part of the screen, select Tools->Resource manager
- Click on img/tilesets and then on the Import button
- Select the walls and floors files from the MV folder (Modern_Interiors->RPG_MAKERS->RPG_MAKER_MV)
- On the upper part of the screen, select Tools->Database, then Tilesets
- Add any of the previously added tilesets to the Tilesets pages A2 for the floors, A4 for the walls.
2)IMPORTING INTERIORS
- On the upper part of the screen, select Tools->Resource manager
- Click on img/tilesets and then on the Import button
- Select any Tileset from the MV Theme_Sorter folder (Modern_Interiors->RPG_MAKERS->RPG_MAKER_MV->Interiors->Theme_Sorter_MV)
- On the upper part of the screen, select Tools->Database, then Tilesets
- Add any of the previously added tilesets to the Tilesets pages B-C-D-E.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
If you look at any of your default B-E tile sheets you will see that they all come in the same specific size 768 x 768 pixels.  That means, in effect, 16 tiles wide and 16 tiles high.
However, that is not how they are shown in the editor.  In the editor they are 8 tiles wide, and everything to the right of that is then shown
underneath
the first half of your tile sheet.  Everything is there, just not where you might expect it to be.

posts.author: Kes
posts.body: What I suspect may be happening is that although the assets were supplied as one image, they are nor formatted as plug and play.  It looks like you have more than one tile sheet's worth of assets there, in which case you will have to arrange them to your satisfaction on two (or more?) sheets in an image program.  However, that is a guess.  What is the exact size (in pixels) of that tile sheet?

posts.author: OroborosGames
posts.body: You are correct! Full size is 768x2532. So if I understand you correctly I only need to snip it into 3 and then I can use it? Would paint be okay for that? xD

posts.author: Kes
posts.body:
Before you just cut it into 3, think carefully about what would be on each one.  If this is your main, or only, tile set for the game then it might not matter, but at least consider if this will give you the optimum layout for your work flow.
As for which program to use - it has to be a program which supports transparency.  I believe that paint.NET does, but that paint does not.  You would have to check.
My recommendation would be to get something like GIMP which is free, and basically has the same functionality as PhotoShop.  You can do all your tile set work in it.
EDIT
I've just looked again at your dimensions.  That sheet is longer than 3 sheets.  Each sheet must be 768 x 768, and 3 x 768 = 2304, not 2532.
